paras.text: Topic: 天氣 The Weather
• Learning to talk about weather conditions, including typhoons.
• Learning to talk about the four seasons and explain why you like or dislike them.
• Learning to compare events.
• Learning to make simple statements about experiences, e.g., trips.
Practice dialogue written for this site with the vocabulary of Dialogue I. The book’s own Dialogue I is on book p. 300; its recording is track 14-01.

lines.zh: 外面風這麼大，我覺得今天比昨天冷多了。臺灣會不會下雪？
lines.py: Wàimiàn fēng zhème dà, wǒ juéde jīntiān bǐ zuótiān lěng duō le. Táiwān huì bú huì xiàxuě?

lines.zh: 平地不會，不過很高的山會下雪，玉山常常下雪。美國呢？開始下雪了嗎？
lines.py: Píngdì bú huì, búguò hěn gāo de shān huì xiàxuě, Yùshān chángcháng xiàxuě. Měiguó ne? Kāishǐ xiàxuě le ma?

lines.zh: 還沒，我們那裡差不多十二月底才開始下雪。冬天真的很冷，我不太喜歡冬天。
lines.py: Hái méi, wǒmen nàlǐ chàbùduō shí'èryuè dǐ cái kāishǐ xiàxuě. Dōngtiān zhēn de hěn lěng, wǒ bú tài xǐhuān dōngtiān.

lines.zh: 我也怕冷，我比較喜歡春天。
lines.py: Wǒ yě pà lěng, wǒ bǐjiào xǐhuān chūntiān.

lines.zh: 春天不錯，不過我覺得秋天更好，天氣很舒服，還可以看紅葉。
lines.py: Chūntiān búcuò, búguò wǒ juéde qiūtiān gèng hǎo, tiānqì hěn shūfú, hái kěyǐ kàn hóngyè.

lines.zh: 我去年秋天在紐約玩了兩個星期。那個時候，天氣很好，紅葉也很漂亮，我玩得很開心。
lines.py: Wǒ qùnián qiūtiān zài Niǔyuē wánle liǎng ge xīngqí. Nàge shíhòu, tiānqì hěn hǎo, hóngyè yě hěn piàoliàng, wǒ wán de hěn kāixīn.

lines.zh: 我在臺灣住了半年多了，有一點想家。
lines.py: Wǒ zài Táiwān zhùle bàn nián duō le, yǒu yìdiǎn xiǎng jiā.

lines.zh: 新年快到了，你想不想回去看父母？
lines.py: Xīnnián kuài dào le, nǐ xiǎng bù xiǎng huíqù kàn fùmǔ?

lines.zh: 想啊，不過我只放五天的假，所以明年夏天才要回去。
lines.py: Xiǎng a, búguò wǒ zhǐ fàng wǔ tiān de jià, suǒyǐ míngnián xiàtiān cái yào huíqù.

lines.zh: 那你今年新年打算做什麼？
lines.py: Nà nǐ jīnnián xīnnián dǎsuàn zuò shénme?

lines.zh: 我想留在臺灣，跟朋友一起過新年，下雪的時候再跟弟弟去山上滑雪。
lines.py: Wǒ xiǎng liú zài Táiwān, gēn péngyǒu yìqǐ guò xīnnián, xiàxuě de shíhòu zài gēn dìdi qù shānshàng huáxuě.

translation.en: It’s so windy outside — I think it’s a lot colder today than yesterday. Does it snow in Taiwan?
Not on the flatlands, but it snows on the high mountains — it snows often on Yushan. What about the US? Has it started snowing there yet?
Not yet. Where I’m from, it usually doesn’t start snowing until around the end of December. Winter is really cold — I don’t like winter that much.
I don’t like the cold either. I like spring better.
Spring’s nice, but I think autumn is even better — the weather is pleasant, and you can go see the red maple leaves.
Last autumn I spent two weeks in New York. The weather was great then, and the leaves were beautiful — I had a wonderful time.
I’ve been living in Taiwan for over half a year now. I’m a little homesick.
New Year is coming up soon — do you want to go back to see your parents?
I do, but I only get five days off, so I won’t go back until next summer.
So what are you planning to do for New Year this time?
I’m planning to stay in Taiwan and spend New Year with friends — and when it snows, go skiing in the mountains with my little brother again.

items.en: Yu Shan (Mount Jade), tallest mountain in central Taiwan

paras.text: Practice dialogue written for this site with the vocabulary of Dialogue II. The book’s own Dialogue II is on book p. 303; its recording is track 14-03.

lines.zh: 如玉，雨下得這麼大，妳怎麼沒帶傘？
lines.py: Rúyù, yǔ xià de zhème dà, nǐ zěnme méi dài sǎn?

lines.zh: 我早上出門的時候還沒下雨，所以沒帶傘。
lines.py: Wǒ zǎoshàng chūmén de shíhòu hái méi xiàyǔ, suǒyǐ méi dài sǎn.

lines.zh: 聽說颱風快要來了。
lines.py: Tīngshuō táifēng kuài yào lái le.

lines.zh: 我已經在新聞上看到了。
lines.py: Wǒ yǐjīng zài xīnwén shàng kàndào le.

lines.zh: 這裡夏天常常有颱風，颱風來的時候，風和雨都很大，出門很不方便。
lines.py: Zhèlǐ xiàtiān chángcháng yǒu táifēng, táifēng lái de shíhòu, fēng hàn yǔ dōu hěn dà, chūmén hěn bù fāngbiàn.

lines.zh: 對啊，到處都濕濕的，我真的很討厭颱風天。
lines.py: Duì a, dàochù dōu shīshī de, wǒ zhēnde hěn tǎoyàn táifēngtiān.

lines.zh: 新聞說這次的颱風比上次的更大，要大家多小心。
lines.py: Xīnwén shuō zhè cì de táifēng bǐ shàng cì de gèng dà, yào dàjiā duō xiǎoxīn.

lines.zh: 希望這次沒有上次那麼可怕。
lines.py: Xīwàng zhè cì méiyǒu shàng cì nàme kěpà.

lines.zh: 妳看，雨好像停了。
lines.py: Nǐ kàn, yǔ hǎoxiàng tíng le.

lines.zh: 太好了！謝謝你借我傘，再見。
lines.py: Tài hǎo le! Xièxie nǐ jiè wǒ sǎn, zàijiàn.

lines.zh: 不客氣，慢走，小心一點。
lines.py: Búkèqì, màn zǒu, xiǎoxīn yìdiǎn.

translation.en: Ruyu, it’s raining so hard — how come you didn’t bring an umbrella?
It hadn’t started raining yet when I left home this morning, so I didn’t bring one.
I heard a typhoon is about to arrive.
I already saw it on the news.
We get typhoons often here in summer. When a typhoon comes, the wind and rain are both really strong, and it’s very inconvenient to go out.
Yeah, everything gets soaking wet everywhere — I really hate typhoon days.
The news said this typhoon is even bigger than the last one, and told everyone to be extra careful.
I hope this one isn’t as scary as the last one.
Look, it seems like the rain has stopped.
Great! Thanks for lending me your umbrella. See you.
You’re welcome. Take care on your way, be careful.

items.en: to be careful, to take care

blocks.en: I. Time-Duration after Verbal 了 le

paras.text: Use: Verb + Time-Duration shows how long a completed activity lasted. If the verb is transitive and takes an object, the verb must be repeated (Verb + Object + Verb + Time-Duration); if the object is moved to the front of the sentence instead, no repetition is needed.

items.zh: 月美在紐約玩了兩個星期。
items.py: Yuèměi zài Niǔyuē wánle liǎng ge xīngqí.
items.en: Yuemei spent two weeks in New York.

items.zh: 我們在家等颱風，等了兩天。
items.py: Wǒmen zài jiā děng táifēng, děngle liǎng tiān.
items.en: We waited at home for the typhoon for two days. (verb repeated — has an object)

items.zh: 這場雨，我們等了半個小時才停。
items.py: Zhè chǎng yǔ, wǒmen děngle bàn ge xiǎoshí cái tíng.
items.en: This rain — we waited half an hour before it stopped. (object fronted — no repetition needed)

blocks.title: 練習 Exercise
blocks.instruction: Complete each sentence with the Verb + Time-Duration pattern, repeating the verb where needed.

items.prompt: 他在玉山上（滑雪）＿＿＿＿＿＿三個鐘頭。

blocks.en: II. Completion-to-date with Double 了 le

paras.text: Use: Verb + 了 + Time-Duration + 了 (“Double 了”) shows how long an action has lasted up to the moment of speaking. The action may or may not still be continuing, depending on context.

items.zh: 這個颱風已經來了兩天了。
items.py: Zhè ge táifēng yǐjīng láile liǎng tiān le.
items.en: This typhoon has already been here for two days.

items.py: Yǔ yǐjīng xiàle yì zhěng tiān le.
items.en: It’s already been raining all day.

items.zh: 我在臺灣住了半年多了。
items.py: Wǒ zài Táiwān zhùle bàn nián duō le.
items.en: I’ve already been living in Taiwan for over half a year.

blocks.title: 練習 Exercise
blocks.instruction: Answer each question using the Double 了 pattern.

items.prompt: 這次的颱風來了多久了？（一天）→ ＿＿＿＿＿＿。
你學滑雪學了多久了？（三個月）→ ＿＿＿＿＿＿。
外面的雨下了多久了？（兩個鐘頭）→ ＿＿＿＿＿＿。

blocks.en: III. 快(要) kuài(yào)…了 le — about to

paras.text: Use: Sentential 了 often appears with adverbs 快, 要, or 快要 to show that something will happen soon — an imminent change of state. In Taiwan, the two-syllable 快要 is preferred when there’s no time word in the sentence; if a specific time word is present, 快要 cannot be used (just 要…了, or the sentence states the time directly).

items.zh: 颱風快要來了，大家要小心。
items.py: Táifēng kuàiyào lái le, dàjiā yào xiǎoxīn.
items.en: The typhoon is about to arrive — everyone should be careful.

items.zh: 快下雪了，你多穿一點衣服。
items.py: Kuài xiàxuě le, nǐ duō chuān yìdiǎn yīfú.
items.en: It’s about to snow — put on some more clothes.

items.zh: 新年快到了，我想回去看父母。
items.py: Xīnnián kuài dào le, wǒ xiǎng huíqù kàn fùmǔ.
items.en: New Year is coming up soon — I want to go back and see my parents.

blocks.title: 練習 Exercise
blocks.instruction: Answer each question about something that will soon happen.

blocks.en: IV. Comparison with 更 gèng — even more so

paras.text: Use: The adverb 更 adds that a fact is even more true than a fact already established — it implies the thing being compared to was already a certain way, and the new one is even more so. 更 is used together with 比, and as an adverb it goes right before the state verb it modifies. Questions about this pattern typically use 是不是.

items.py: Jīnnián dōngtiān bǐ qùnián gèng lěng.
items.en: This winter is even colder than last winter. (last winter was already cold)

items.zh: 這次的颱風比上次的更大。
items.py: Zhè cì de táifēng bǐ shàng cì de gèng dà.
items.en: This typhoon is even bigger than the last one.

items.zh: 我覺得秋天比春天更舒服。
items.py: Wǒ juéde qiūtiān bǐ chūntiān gèng shūfú.
items.en: I think autumn is even more pleasant than spring.

blocks.title: 練習 Exercise
blocks.instruction: Ask a question about each pair using 是不是…比…更….

items.prompt: 紐約的冬天／臺北的冬天（冷）→ ＿＿＿＿＿＿？

blocks.en: V. Inferior Comparison with 沒有 méiyǒu…那麼/這麼 nàme/zhème…

paras.text: Use: A 沒有 B 那麼/這麼 + state verb says A is not as [adjective] as B. This pattern is almost always negative; 那麼/這麼 can sometimes be dropped. Its positive counterpart, A 有 B 那麼/這麼 + state verb, is rare except in 嗎 questions. Note the three-way contrast: A 跟 B 一樣 (equal, Lesson 13), A 沒有 B 那麼 (inferior), A 比 B (superior, Lesson 8). Questions use the A-not-A form (有沒有).

items.zh: 今年的颱風沒有去年的那麼可怕。
items.py: Jīnnián de táifēng méiyǒu qùnián de nàme kěpà.
items.en: This year’s typhoon isn’t as scary as last year’s.

items.zh: 春天沒有秋天這麼舒服。
items.en: Spring isn’t as pleasant as autumn.

items.zh: 紐約的冬天沒有臺北的冬天那麼濕。
items.py: Niǔyuē de dōngtiān méiyǒu Táiběi de dōngtiān nàme shī.
items.en: Winter in New York isn’t as wet as winter in Taipei.

blocks.title: 練習 Exercise
blocks.instruction: Answer each question using 沒有…那麼/這麼….

items.prompt: 今天的風有沒有昨天那麼大？（否）→ ＿＿＿＿＿＿。
滑雪有沒有游泳這麼難學？（否）→ ＿＿＿＿＿＿。
這次的假有沒有上次那麼長？（否，只放五天）→ ＿＿＿＿＿＿。

paras.text: Goal: Learning to describe the four seasons and explain why you like or dislike them.
Task: Tell the class about the climate of your home country. Which season do you like the most, and which the least? Why? (因為…所以…)

blocks.en: II. How Long Did You Live There?

paras.text: Goal: Learning to make simple statements about your experiences.
Task: Ask your classmates where they have lived and how long they lived in each place. Record your findings and report to the class, e.g. 安同在西班牙住了多久？ 安同在西班牙住了兩個月（了）。
Goal: Learning to make comparisons between events.
Task: Compare the average temperatures of Taipei in the various seasons of last year and this year, using the patterns 比、更、比較、比…更、跟…一樣、沒有…那麼 introduced in this and earlier lessons.
Goal: Learning to compare weather conditions.

Task: Earlier you learned what the climate is like in a classmate’s home country. Compare the climate there with your own in more detail — spring, summer, autumn, winter, whether there are typhoons, whether it rains often, and whether it snows — and record the results on a chart.
Goal: Learning to discuss events and activities in summer.
Task: Discuss with a classmate what summer in Taiwan is like — the weather, the fruit people often eat, and the things people often do — and write down your findings in Chinese.

A “typhoon day” is a break from school and work announced when a typhoon with strong enough winds is expected to hit an area within the next few hours; school and work are called off until the storm passes.

Because a typhoon's heavy wind and rain can make daily life genuinely unsafe, the power to call off work and school was given to a government agency back in the early 1990s. That agency weighs the official weather forecast together with suggestions from local governments when making the call. Today the decision is no longer made for the whole country at once — it has been handed over to regional governments instead, so one city can call a typhoon day while its neighbor doesn't. To find out whether school or work is cancelled where you are, check the local news or the relevant government website.

items: I can talk about weather conditions, including typhoons.
I can describe the four seasons and explain why I like or dislike them.
I can make simple statements about experiences, e.g., trips.
